newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to privatize its first state bank Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to privatize its first state bank Thursday.

text.p: Banerj, the first Brazilian state bank to be privatized, will go on sale today with the country's two largest private banks bidding on the auction.
Bradesco and Banco Itau are the only investors which will participate in the closed-envelope privatization auction of the Rio de Janeiro state bank at 1600 local/1800 GMT, Rio officials said.

The other six pre-qualified investors -- Banco BBA Creditanstalt, Bank of Boston Brazil unit, General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corporation, Banco CCF do Brasil, Companhia de Investimentos Latino-Americana and Golden Cross -- have dropped out of the running.
Banerj had been due to be sold off on December 17 but the sale was postponed after a court issued an injunction that blocked the sale.

The new date for the privatization was set after the Rio de Janeiro state government succeeded in lifting the court injunction granted to the Association of Banerj's Employees, an opponent of the sell-off.

Although the state government has succeeded in lifting this injunction, the possibility of new court orders which may prevent the bank from being sold off at the last minute is not completely ruled out.

Rio de Janeiro's Banking Workers Union is reported to also have appealed the court asking for the suspension of the sell-off, but no court decision has been made yet, according to the Rio de Janeiro Planning office.
Banerj and its insurance firm Banerj Seguros will be auctioned off for a minimum price of 436.693 million reais and 43.310 million reais, respectively, on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
Investors will have to acquire the bank and its insurer together, which means that bids totalling less than 480 million reais will not be accepted.

The bidders will be allowed to pay off 30 million reais -- 27 million reais of Banerj's base price and 3.0 million reais of the insurer's base price -- in Privatization Certificates, which represent state securitized debt.
The state also clarified it will assume the debts Banerj owes to its pension fund, Previ-Banerj.
The debts had been seen making investors wary of the Banerj sale.

Since early January Banerj has been administered by private bank Bozano, Simonsen, hired to run the bank and prepare it for sell-off on behalf of the Central Bank, which took over Banerj in December 1994.
Bozano has received 36 million reais for the job and will be paid five percent of the auction's receipts.

Banerj bank has a net worth of 180 million reais and total assets of 4.0 billion reais. Under Bozano's management, Banerj's staff was cut to 8,226 employees from 11,970 employees in December 1995 and 27 branches were closed, reducing the bank's branch network to 193.
